Subject: Potential publisher partnership + bundled distribution with VectorFlow

Hi Camila,

Thanks for taking a look. SableAI has been fielding strong demand from ISVs for a lightweight licensed distribution of our base models (no fine-tune weights). VectorFlow approached us interested in bundling a hosted inference offering + customer-managed weights access for enterprise accounts.

We think a co-distribution play with Redwood would accelerate reach while giving publishers proper controls on weights access and attribution. High level asks from our side:
- conditional weights access for Tier 2+ partners only (audited use, NDA plus data use restrictions)
- simple attribution and commercial terms (rev share or one-time licensing fee)
- a short pilot to validate the integration and packaging (1 quarter)

Amit is looped in from VectorFlow to explain the ISV integration model. Would you be open to a short call early next week to sketch a mutual action plan and identify legal items? I attached a SOC2 summary and our initial term sheet (non-final).

Best,

Thanks Camila — Tuesday works. To answer your questions briefly:
- Conditional access model: We prefer a contract-bound access token model for enterprise customers; transient download-only for escrow is possible but adds complexity.
- Versioning: We'd like to offer pinned major versions for pilot participants and allow patch updates on a case-by-case basis.
- SLAs: For the bundle, baseline is 99.5% uptime on hosted endpoints; VectorFlow wants latency under 120ms p50 for common workloads.

Attached is a lightly redlined term sheet (v1_redlined) that reflects license options (per-seat vs. rev share), attribution clauses, and an exclusivity request limited to specific industry verticals. Sergio — appreciate any early legal flags.

Looking forward to the call.

Maria / Camila — quick legal read and suggested guardrails:

1) Conditional access approach looks sensible but we need clarity on "vetted partner's enterprise customers" — include a definition (e.g., customers must sign a partner-specific Addendum).
2) Escrow vs transient access: Redwood can support ephemeral token-based access tied to customer entitlements (preferred). Permanent download requires escrow + separate indemnity.
3) Exclusivity: our standard position is to avoid platform-level exclusivity. If Sable wants vertical carveouts, cap duration to the pilot period + 6 months.
4) Attribution and branding: agree on co-branding guidelines; we prefer a lightweight attribution footer and a shared partner page.
5) Revenue split: propose two options to test in pilot — (A) 70/30 revenue share to publisher for direct-license deals; (B) fixed license fee for reseller bundles.

I'll send a marked term sheet back with these annotations. Also proposing an internal MAP template (attached) to align GTM, success criteria, and technical integration owners.

Sergio Alvarez
Head of Legal, Redwood Inference
